Huber's robust regression

Synopsis


use oakleaf

  type, abstract, public :: robfun_function
   contains
     procedure(fvalue), deferred :: val
     procedure(fgradient), deferred :: grad
     procedure :: fungrad => fungradient
     procedure :: hess => fhessian
     procedure :: maxalf => maxalpha
  end type bfgs_function

  abstract interface

     real(REAL64) function fvalue(this,x)
       import :: REAL64, bfgs_function
       class(bfgs_function), intent(in) :: this
       real(REAL64), dimension(:), intent(in) :: x
     end function fvalue

     subroutine fgradient(this,x,fgrad)
       import :: REAL64, bfgs_function
       class(bfgs_function), intent(in) :: this
       real(REAL64), dimension(:), intent(in) :: x
       real(REAL64), dimension(:), intent(out) :: fgrad
     end subroutine fgradient

  end interface

subroutine huberfit(fcn,x,H,gtol,maxiter,verbose,report_file,iflag)

    class(bfgs_function), intent(in) :: fcn
    real(REAL64), dimension(:), intent(in out) :: x
    real(REAL64), dimension(:,:), intent(out) :: H
    real(REAL64), intent(in) :: gtol
    integer, intent(in) :: maxiter
    logical, intent(in) :: verbose
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: report_file
    integer, intent(out) :: iflag

end subroutine huberfit

Description

The subroutine huberfit estimates parameters of a model by the method of the maximum likelihood with the robust Huber's function. It is implemented based on the BFGS method.

The function does to approximate the data yi ≈ f(xi; p) for i = 1, …, N points by the function f(.) with an optimal choice of a vector of parameters p. The user must supply the value f(.), its gradient 𝛻 f(x) and a data set. The scale s, a slack variable, is added and the robust likelihood estimate is made by search of a minimum of the function

log L({xi,yi};p) = 1/N ∑ ϱ{[yi - f(xi;p)] / s} + log s.

Robust methods suppose s > 0, as the consequence, they does not converge for data without statistical errors (rounding errors are not enough). If the state is recognised, the solution continues with the constrain s = 1 set.

Statistical errors of parameters are estimated based on the inverse Hessian in the minimum. Its estimate by BFSG method is rough, the accuracy is about ~10%.

The regression is suitable for fully determined problems without constrains. As BFGS method can fail for non-decreasing functions, like functions of Tukey or Hampel, the only the Huber function is implemented. No leverage points are sanitised and data should be winsorised prior to use, i.e. data must not contain IEEE Nans and Infs and far data should be replaced by an order value, else such data can significantly affect the solution. If the assumptions are met, the results are both stable and reliable.

For details, see Oakleaf's User guide.

Parameters

fcn
[in] is an abstract function carrying the value of the function and the gradient. See below for details.
x,y
[in] Arrays of data.
par
[in out] The initial estimates on the input, and results on the output.
parerr
[out] The estimates of statistical errors of the parameters.
scale
[in out] The robust scale. The estimate should be given on the input.
stdsig
[out] The standard deviation
H
[out] an approximation the quasi-Hessian in minimum
gtol
[in] the tolerance for the convergence finish as the Euclidean norm of the gradient. The square root of machine epsilon (10-8) is safe choice, if elements of the gradient are small, value about 10-13 is enough.
maxiter
[in] The maximal amount of iterations. Recommended value is about two hundredth per variable. Usually a few thousands is enough.
verbose
[in] Be, or not to be, verbose.
report_file
[in] A file to store intermediate steps, if a non-empty string is passed. Consult the program listing for details.
iflag
[out] A result flag; the values 0,1 indicates success, value 6 is a fail. For details, see BFGS method. If it fails, the output values must be considered undefined.

The implementation is in src/huberfit.f08.

The function

The minimised function is defined as a derived type object. The user must specify its functional value f(x) and the gradient 𝛻 f(x). Note, user specifies f(x), not the likelihood function log L(x;p). If data are required, they are stored in the derived type, see the example below.

fcn % val()
Returns the functional value f(xi) at the point xi.
fcn % grad()
The gradient 𝛻 f(xi) at the point xi.

Example

We wish to estimate of parameters a,b of a line by the robust regression. The function implementation should have been in the module, to generate the external interface. Save the program to the file rline.f08: 

module the_function

  use oakleaf
  use iso_fortran_env
  implicit none

  type, extends(huberfit_function) :: line_function
   contains
     procedure :: val => lvalue
     procedure :: grad => lgradient
  end type line_function

contains

  function lvalue(this,x,p) result(fval)
    class(line_function) :: this
    real(REAL64), intent(in) :: x
    real(REAL64), dimension(:), intent(in) :: p
    real(REAL64) :: fval
    real(REAL64) :: a, b

    a = p(1)
    b = p(2)
    fval = a*x + b

  end function lvalue

  subroutine lgradient(this,x,p,fgrad)
    class(line_function) :: this
    real(REAL64), intent(in) :: x
    real(REAL64), dimension(:), intent(in) :: p
    real(REAL64), dimension(:), intent(out) :: fgrad

    fgrad(1) = x
    fgrad(2) = 1

  end subroutine lgradient

end module the_function

program what_about_rline

  use oakleaf
  use the_function
  use iso_fortran_env
  implicit none

  real(REAL64), dimension(5), target :: x = [ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 ]
  real(REAL64), dimension(5),target :: y = [ 1.1, 2.2, 3.3, 4.2, 5.5 ]
  type(line_function), target :: fcn
  real(REAL64), dimension(2) :: p, perr
  real(REAL64), dimension(2,2) :: H
  real(REAL64) :: s, stdsig, gtol
  integer :: iflag,i

  ! initial scale estimate, s > 0
  s = 1

  ! initial parameters estimate, p = [ a, b ]
  p = 0


  gtol = sqrt(epsilon(gtol))

  call huberfit(fcn,x,y,p,perr,stdsig,s,H,gtol,2*200, &
       .true.,'',iflag)
  write(error_unit,*) 'huberfit iflag=',iflag
  write(error_unit,*) 'scale=',s,' stdsig=',stdsig

  do i = 1,2
     write(error_unit,*) i,': p=',p(i),'+-',perr(i)
  end do

   write(*,*) 'residuals: ', y - (p(1)*x + p(2))

end program what_about_rline
